Overview / Operations / Teams & Crews
Resource accountability

Know the people and equipment behind the callsign.

Team records bring together staffing, capabilities, vehicles, aircraft, equipment, current status, and activity. Operations can see whether a resource is ready for the next assignment and what it is doing now.

Team detail

One resource, several connected views.

The team detail window adapts to the resource type. A ground team, aircrew, UAS crew, K9 team, or utility team sees the relevant personnel and equipment context.

PersonnelAircrewEquipmentVehiclesAircraftLogs
Resource types

Describe capability without hiding accountability.

Team type shapes the detail view, while assignment and status show what that resource is doing.

Readiness and status

Availability is an operational fact.

A team can be available, assigned, briefed, en route, on scene, returning, resting, or out of service. The current status belongs beside its assignment and its staffing.

  • Review composition and qualifications before tasking.
  • See assigned vehicles, aircraft, and equipment.
  • Record movement, rest, and changes to availability.
Activity history

Every status change has context.

Task, status, unit, and activity logs keep the team’s work traceable. Follow the record from briefing through return and use it when writing the incident narrative.

Tasks & assignments →Documentation →
A resource across modules

The team record follows the team.

Staffing and equipment affect readiness. The assignment establishes what the team is doing. Field status and activity become part of its history.
